text_fidelity_a:
Contigo Fit Autospout Water Bottle 32oz, Surge When I examined this water bottle's product picture, I wrongly assumed that it was constructed of stainless steel like my other Contigo water bottle because, in appearance, they look exactly the same, with the same dark color. Unfortunately, this water bottle is made of plastic, inside and out.

The claim from the manufacturer is that this plastic is BPA free. Perhaps this will be reassuring enough for many consumers to be willing to purchase this water bottle. However, my understanding, based on my own personal research on the subject, is that there is no such thing as any type of plastic that does not to some extent leach chemicals into any water one puts into a plastic container. So plastic water bottles are a problem for me. However, since the manufacturer did not outright lie about the plastic, only buried it in the bowels of the product description such that I completely missed it, I will not strongly downgrade my rating for that.

There is another issue with this water bottle, though, that is also an issue for me personally. The lid requires one to suck water out through a short, straw-like top. This will require use of a straw-cleaning, slender brush in order to adequately clean it, and the manufacturer does not provide such a brush along with this water bottle.

The lid will also need to be soaked in warm, soapy dishwater along with the water bottle itself after every use in order to avoid the build-up of mold. However, since every water bottle is ideally treated that way, I will not grade down this water bottle for needing to be washed very carefully.

The one advantage a plastic water bottle has over a stainless steel one is that, in some cases, it can be lighter in weight. I will admit that my stainless steel Contigo water bottle is heavier in weight than this plastic one. But the way to prevent that from being a problem is to simply not fill a stainless-steel water bottle completely full, or, better yet, purchase one that isn't huge and unwieldy in size.
text_fidelity_b: Contigo Fit Autospout Water Bottle 32oz, Surge

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds This tent was packaged well. Easy to follow directions and was very simple to set up. I am an Eagle Scout and have been camping for over 35 years so the tent was pretty intuitive to set up. It says "Weathertec - guarenteed to keep you dry" on the outside. I read everything for sealing instructions prior to taking this to the woods. No requirements for sealing included and in fact it said all seams taped. I felt pretty confident. The weekend was calling for temps in the 50's and rain (not hard... just drizzle). I opened and tested the setup prior to camp. It was easy and seemed large enough. I took it out and had it set in approximately 30 seconds. The tent was spacious for two 6'2 guys and gear (cots) sleeping gear small packs and room to spare. It was shorter than expected and a bit smaller than I hoped... topping off about 5'5" at a guess and very tight with a cot (it touched the wall on both ends). The worst was the rain. It held up well to the first 1/2 hour or so but soon it was leaking. By 2am... it was damp... by morning there was about a cup of water in the floor. And the walls were soaked. The bathtub floor retained all the water. It leaked very badly. From seemingly every pore. The second night I spent alone in the dead center. Sleeping bag was soaked the tent was soaked and everything I had was damp even though it was in a chair or on a cot. It took over a day to dry the tent out to ship it back. All this from a light drizzle. Less than 1/2 inch of rain over two days. The firewood on the ground outside was dryer than the personals in my tent. On a scale of 1-10 Ease of set up 10, keeping out bugs 10, big windows 10... this could be a great shelter on a clear day but waterproof 1.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds

Vivid Sports Rainbow Graphite Pickleball Paddle Set, Polymer Honeycomb Core, 1 Neoprene Paddle Cover, Paddle for Men, Women, Children, Supporting The Human Rights Organization, USA Pickleball Approved This is an OK paddle. I don't love it, I don't hate it. I think my favorite thing about this paddle is the colorful design on the paddle face.

The face itself has almost no texture/grit, which as a brand new player may not matter, but will quickly become important after you get the hang of hitting the ball. The paddle face is approximately ~0.5 inches (~13 mm), which is on the thinner side. The upside of a thin paddle is that it provides more power than a thicker paddle, but on the downside, it will be tougher to spin with it (which is compounded by the fact the paddle face has no texture).

Another thing I didn't like was the handle--it feels flat, like a piece of wood. Round handles are much more comfortable in my experience. The grip, however, was pretty nice. It is soft and comfortable to hold, and absorbs sweat pretty well. An added bonus with this paddle is that it comes with a paddle cover. Not a huge deal, but a nice touch nonetheless.

My bottom line is that this is a decent first paddle. Otherwise, I would pass.

text_fidelity_a:
Gempestoer Mini Personal Water Filter for Hiking Outdoor Mountaineering, Backpacking, Hunting, Field Military Training, Camping, Travel, and Emergency Preparedness (Green) Has anyone tried this? The main filtering aspect seems good, which to me is the most important. But if you are buying this because of the extras, be careful. Here are the details:
--WHISTLE: it works, on or off the filter tube. It twists on/off. Be sure to keep track of it. LOUD.
--COMPASS: Mine doesn't work. It won't adjust to correct direction, or any direction. It doesn't move, period. I had it side by side with one of my other compasses, and it did nothing. Bummer.
--MIRROR: The flip side of the compass has a mirror, for signaling etc. Twist off compass end to access. Very clear, looks good. Slightly smaller than size of a quarter.
--D-ring clip: mediocre, might want something else. It is attached via a basic "key ring", which is then attached through the molded plastic piece on the tube.
--STRAW: this includes a piece of rubber tubing for attaching to filter and using as a straw- either in a bottle, or to add length for being able to access a water source. Will need to figure out way to carry this separately (dont lose it!). Basic tubing size, so should be easy to replace or buy longer tubing.
--FILTER: all points to it working!
OK, back to the filter. I used it on tap water. I suppose I could have wandered out to my creek and grabbed some water. Maybe I will still do that. While our tap water tastes fine, it is noticeably different compared to our on board fridge water filter. I tried this is a mason jar with tap water. I followed directions (blow first to exhaust, then gently draw up water). I could tell how silky smooth the water tasted with no other tastes coming through. I then took a sip of the tap water without the filter straw and could note the "flavor". So this straw is filtering something for sure.

I have lifestraws, and now this. I am a big fan of redundancy and variety, and the saying "two is one and one is none". I keep straws in my "bug out bag", and truck "get home bag". I have even kept on in my purse. Must have for hiking bag. Having viable water source is #1 for me. These things aren't too expensive, so I find it an easy, budget friendly addition to emergency preparedness. The price is spot on for a single straw. Wish the compass worked.
text_fidelity_b: Gempestoer Mini Personal Water Filter for Hiking Outdoor Mountaineering, Backpacking, Hunting, Field Military Training, Camping, Travel, and Emergency Preparedness (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
cycmoto Anne Kids Bike for Toddlers and Kids, 14 16 Inch Girls Bike for 3-7 Years Old with Training Wheels and Basket, Pink, Yellow The bike arrived in good shape. Nothing was dented up and it was a reasonably smooth assembly. The tires arrived with enough air to get a few test rides in, but I wouldn't assume this to always be true and you will need to add air to the tires.

The listing states a novice can assemble this bike in 15 minutes. Unless you assemble bikes for a living it will take you longer than 15 minutes. However, this is the second bike I've assembled lately and the cycmoto was definitely easier. It will take you about 10 minutes just to unbox and remove all the foam and plastic ties. Then you will want to spend at least 10 minutes skimming through the instructions to brief yourself on the tasks at hand. I spent about 20 minutes getting all the necessary pieces together and partially tightened. Then I spent another 30 minutes adjusting, straightening, leveling and right sizing the seat, handlebars and brakes. You will want to refer to the instructions when adjusting the front brake. I did not install the training wheels, the basket or the splash guards (see comments below). So, if you just plan to assemble just the main pieces you should expect to spend about 75 minutes. If you plan to install all the extras then you should add another 30 minutes.

It comes with a flat metal multi tool and a dual size Allen wrench that can be used to completely assemble. I used the included tools to assemble. It was a little difficult for certain bolts, but it can be done. The only additional tool I used that was not included was a simple Phillips head screwdriver.

You should note that this bike has front and back hand brakes and not a coaster brake (if you pedal backwards it will spin backwards freely and not brake). The front brake (right handlebar) has two pads that squeeze the wheel to stop. The back brake (left handlebar) has a different stopping mechanism that is build into the crank system. The one concern I have with the brakes is that they are plastic. I hope they don't crack or break if the bike falls. Learning to use the hand brakes early could be better if you think the kid will grow into a mountain or bmx style bike.

A few things to note:

1) the instructions did not include a section for installing the splash guards. I am fairly confident I know which guard goes in the front/back by looking at the pictures in the listing. It would have been nice to have this in the instructions.

2) there are instructions for installing the basket, but I am either missing parts (the plate, small metal sheets and screws) or the instructions should be updated to describe attaching the basket using a ziptie like piece that was included. Personally, I would like to attach the basket as described in the instructions, but those parts were not included.

I did not install either the basket or splash guards. These are advanced attachments that should be used for kids who already know how to ride a bike with two wheels or if you plan to use training wheels. If you are purchasing this bike to train someone how to ride without training wheels then you should assume there will be a fall or two. By waiting to attach the splash guards and the basket you will avoid damaging while practicing to learn to ride a bike.

I would recommend not using the training wheels at all because it could make training without them more difficult. However, uou can adjust the height of the training wheels. So, if you start with the training wheels completely on the grown then you can slowly raise them off the ground.

Overall, the bike looks nice and feels solid.

This bike is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: cycmoto Anne Kids Bike for Toddlers and Kids, 14 16 Inch Girls Bike for 3-7 Years Old with Training Wheels and Basket, Pink, Yellow

Amazon's price currently beat the online horse supply stores I had previously purchased from and I went with graphite and french blue colors and they are really nice.

If he had to wear a halter full time I would have gotten a single-layer nylon adjustable halter with just rings instead of these very heavy D-shaped rings, just so he'd have something lighter.

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex TC5000 Treadclimber (Discontinued) Bottom line is, if someone asked me if I would 'recommend', I would pause and struggle. Well...I wouldn't NOT recommend..afterall, I do sweat in a hurry; it does get your heart going; it doesn't take up much space; it is built well; it does give you a few variations of usage. Unfortunately, I can't comment on what results I get because I don't USE IT enough to really know. By the same token, I cannot comment on anything mechanical either, for the same reason.

We all have our own reasons for NOT using something and certainly most can relate to having fitness equipment that collects dust, or clothes! So when friends or family members ask me why I don't use mine, other than all the personal excuses, the reasons are this:

I find that I have to be so careful how I walk and how I place each and every step I make on this machine, or it occasionally twists my knee around. I cannot explain it in writing, but it's so frequent that it does this that I spend all my time concentrating on walking so that I'm unaffected! If I don't, I have had it jerk my knee, my ankles and it of course affects everything on up - back, hips, etc.
It doesn't seem to make any difference whether I use the treadles, or lock them together to use as treadmill. In fact, when I use the treadles, I find that i have to walk with somewhat of a straddle to give equal weight proportion to the motion otherwise your motion is something equivalent to walking with one high heel shoe on and one off. So, the very way that you step manipulates the treadles.
All this completely takes away from enjoying the use of the machine and it becomes a chore for me. I have other things I want to concentrate on than each and every step I make, and being so cautious! I mean, who wants that?!

Funny, I have read every review and every comment and don't see anyone else mentioning these things and I'm not sure why not. My sister and a friend jumped on my machine and they could completely see what I was talking about. Is it just my machine? I don't know. I purchased mine directly from Bowflex and paid a bundle more than this price showing on Amazon, btw!

Again, it isn't that I DON'T recommend this item, but for me, anyway, I would probably get more enjoyment, more usage, and therefore greater results, for FAR LESS money using something else.

While we haven't had opportunity to camp with them yet, I have tested the product out in the house.

At first, I wasn't sure about the inflation, but being inexperienced with this type of product, I really didn't know what to expect (would it inflate like an air mattress, or would inflation be minimal?). When I first unrolled it, it didn't seem to inflate, even after the 3-5 minutes described in the instructions. Then I realized I unrolled it with the valve closed, and the instructions state to unroll with the valve open. So, I rolled it back, squeezing out what air had entered it, then proceeded to unroll again with the valve open. After several minutes, I came back, put it on the floor and tested it. It had inflated significantly more (don't expect an air mattress), though still remained thin. For me it was fairly comfortable on its own, and with my sleeping bag on top of it, it was more than comfortable enough for camping.

After testing it for comfort on the hard floor in my house, I rolled it back up, and a lot of air came out. It was easy to roll and easily went back into its carry bag, which is a big plus (too many products never fit back in their original packaging).

So, short of knowing how it would do on the ground outside in cold weather, I'd say this product was worth the purchase. It seems to be made of high-quality material, and it provides added comfort for sleeping in a sleeping bag.
text_fidelity_b: Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot

text_fidelity_a: Mountainsmith Day Lumbar Pack One of my favorite bags.  I bought this one for a family trip to Walt Disney World so I could be the family pack mule. I can wear it on my hips and twist it around as-needed.  Sometimes I'd wear it on my side for accessibility; most times on my butt behind me.  Sometimes I'd spin it around to the front to wear in my lap on rides.  Also, if you get tired of carrying it on your hips, I also used it as a cross-shoulder bag. Once I really had the bag loaded heavy and it got tiring on my hips --- for those rare scenarios, you can also use the should strap as additional support while on your hips, too. I can see how this bag would be great for hikers, tourists, beachgoers, visiting amusement parks, etc.  It's worth noting that while there is a ton of storage, you can also cinch-up the straps and only put a little bit of stuff in there and the bag compacts a bit.  I bought a D-Clip for the molle loops to secure my hat/visor when not in use and I also used that looped yellow-cord on the front more than I thought for my sweat towel or to hang my kids' towel or hats.

B7 Smart Bracelet Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate /Blood Pressure/Sleep Monitor ,Smart Watch for iOS /Andriod Phone，Smart Watch Bracelet for Men /Women I have lived with this tracker for several weeks now. All the features that I use seem to work well but some nights the sleep doesn't fully track. I was looking for something to just record the step & sleep tracking to enter into my work health tracking & occasionally check my heart rate for fun. I don't use the email, camera or music features.

The band is pretty comfortable & pliable but it kind of looks like an old swatch. I was a little self conscious about that at first but I noticed that other fit trackers also looked like that & I forgot about it over time. The crystal over the watch face is very durable, I have used it during all kinds of work & activities & there are no big scratches. The instructions said not to use the watch in the shower but I did almost immediately with no issues.

All of the watch features are accessed through a touch point on the face either with a short or long touch. The touch sensor is sensitive enough that it changes (& buzzes) when I fold my arms or tuck it under when I sleep. The battery lasts about 4 days. The charger is unusual in form & is as large as the watch face so it isn't ideal to carry around.

The Wearfit app from the QR code connects to the phone easily & records data reliably. The app does show ads at the bottom which is annoying & sometimes the data is displayed a little buggy. The app also uses a lot of battery when it is up. I wish it fed to the Google fit app because then I wouldn't have to enter the data for my company's site. I really dislike that the app has ads.

text_fidelity_a:
Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor I have not previously worked with Old Timer knives, though I have had my share of pocket knives that have served me well. So, this is my first experience with this brand and so far I am very pleased. This is a quality pocket knife, without a lot of frills and fancy features but very well made and attractive.

Most cheap pocket knives have a plastic handle, spring-assisted fly-out blade, and a locking mechanism. Beyond that the features become quite varied and bring different features to the table. That's all good, but anything beyond the basics - a blade in a case - adds weight and size. This knife is different. It keeps everything very simple - a single pull-out blade that locks. That's it.

The blade is solid and sharp right out of the package and is well suited for most tasks. There is no wobble in the blade and it remains stiff and tight, which is a good thing. The blade is free of pits and dings (at least initially) and is sharp enough to cut without pain (so be careful).

The handle is bone, not cheap plastic or resin. It has a nice, solid feel to it and it will last for decades with proper care. It also has eye appeal and is reminiscent of old-fashioned knives.

I am very pleased with this knife and will carry it instead of a larger cheap knife when I want a small, lightweight but well-made knife with me. I expect to get years of service from this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Camp Creek 6-Person Tent (WARNING- This is an IN DEPTH review for those serious about making buying decisions. If you prefer a quick summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
----------------
My family has been very enthusiastic about tent camping for quite some time. We have had a variety of tents over time, but one of our favorites was a Eureka one we had that was vintage. It was one of the last ones made in the US from what we understand and it lasted for a long time even past us getting it used. The design was perfect for the family and it was sturdy too. Had my husband not refused to stake it down one night insisting we would not get any wind, we would probably still have it. We got wind that night- so much that it pinned him against the building it blew him up against. He never refused again.

Our most recent tent experience has been horrible. We got a fantastic Coleman tent- great design- but the poles snapped the second time we used it- no wind, no bad weather- just snapped.

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
This tent is the most like the design of the Eureka we had some years ago that we have seen yet. I am going to break this down into sections about this tent so it is easier to work through to find what you want to know.

FABRIC
The fabric in this tent is as nice or nicer than the Colemans that we have had. It is gray, white, and teal. The screen is no-see-um netting but is thin- care needs to be taken to be sure it does not tear.

POLES
The poles are fantastic- best feature of this tent. The side poles are heavy steel with steel core shock cords in the poles. There are several shock corded fiberglass poles in this set. These poles go on top for a curved roof and also for the curved fly.

CONNECTORS
The connectors are all plastic, but quite sturdy- better than some of Coleman. Over time, I am not sure how they will hold up, but they are nice and sturdy.

STAKES
The stakes are about 8 inches long with a curved hook on top. They are about 1/4 inch thick straight rounded steel stakes- not something you will want to use in high winds or soil that is extremely wet or sandy. If you want something a little substantial or longer, you will have to purchase them. There are 13 stakes that come with this- for the tent and the cords that hold the tent stable.

WINDOWS
There is screen on the ceiling of the tent for a lot of circulation. It breathes nicely. The windows are also nice and large. However, one of my problems with this tent is that there are no ties for the windows to roll them up. They have to hang loose. I am not fond of that and wish they would have put ties or clips on them.

DOOR
There is a tie back for the door, but not the window in the door. The door is plenty roomy and opens nicely. It is not too far above the ground and opens with a nice zipper. If it were reinforced like some of the Coleman tents (with a little curved fiberglass pole around the edge and velcro to shut it as you go in and out) it would be perfect. Still it is pretty nice.

STAND UP ROOM
Everyone in the family has plenty of room to stand up straight including our 6 ft 3in member of the family.

SET UP
The set up of the tent is not difficult but it does take at least two people. If this is going to be put up in any kind of breeze, you will need three or four people to hold the tent from blowing away while you try to get it set up and staked down.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions are a nylon label sewn into the case. They are not particularly detailed when it comes to the extras like how to put the hanging storage in the tent. It is adequate for how to put up the tent, however, not a lot of detail beyond that.

CASE
Many times a tent comes in a very tiny case that does not store the tent once you have used it because the tent is often too big once it is rolled back up again. In this case, with some work, the case does fit the tent without too much struggle. It has a dual zipper. The tent comes with tiny ties in it that should be more substantial to help put the tent back.

FLY
The fly goes on well and does clip into place nicely.

WIND
Although this is difficult to put up in the wind (ask me how I know), once it is up and staked down with the lines and stakes and everything clipped as it should be, this tent is quite nice even in the wind. It stays pretty well although I would not expect it to make it through a very severe wind storm which most tents will not. For the usual weather, it seems to do fine.

WATERPROOF?
I did not have any experience with rain- the entire time the tent was set up, there was no rain. I will have to update about that.

PRIVACY
The top of this tent is white and quite thin. If you want privacy, you might want to keep in mind that you can probably see through it at night with a light on. The windows are a good height if you plan to sleep in a cot, mattress, or sleeping bag.

DURABILITY
Of course, I can only answer this over time, but so far, the construction of this tent is impressive, as long as you put down a tarp to protect the floor and keep applying waterproofing.

WEIGHT
This tent is made to stand up- that means that the poles are sturdy and strong. They are HEAVY. That means that this is a substantial package to carry. It is not for backpacking, but it will be a great base to set up if you are going out climbing or exploring with a small backpack tent.

WHAT I WISH THEY HAD DONE
I wish they had put ties on the windows. As small as that sounds, I think it matters in a tent situation. I also wish that they had a hook or ring coming down from the center of the ceiling to hang a lantern or light from.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite a few minor changes I would prefer, this is a nice tent. The poles are a great design and made to be strong. The package comes with everything you need to set up a sturdy nice tent, but you may want to purchase better stakes. A great comfortable tent for two to four people ( six if you are like sardines) if you keep up on treating for being waterproof, this tent could last some time if you take care of it. We love the design as a whole and are glad to have this.

MY RATING
Even though I would like a few different things with this- like tie backs on the windows, hook on the ceiling or even a reinforced door like Colemans have, None of these are enough to give it under five stars. The basic structure is great and hopefully will last longer than others on the market these days.

UPDATES
If you have a question about this tent that I have not addressed in this review, I will be happy to update if I can. Also, once we use it again next year I will update as well since we are approaching winter now.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Camp Creek 6-Person Tent

Camplux Propane Camping Stove 2 Burner, Portable Gas Stoves with Regulator for Outdoor Cooking Total Power at 14,000 BTU We had some company for the summer for a few weeks. Having access to a small grill was important for the young adults.

LIGHTWEIGHT
This is not paper weight by any means, but it is light weight enough that it is easy to move and relocate.

DOES IT SIT FIRMLY?
This has to have a stand, stable surface or a table top to use it. It is pretty sturdy.

USE
This is electronic ignition and the center burner has to be lit with a lighter. Be sure to have one handy if you plan to use it.

They did not have any issues with operating the burners. They are big enough to put a decent pan on. A simple cast iron skillet (8-10 inches) fit well on the burner.

GRILL
The grill was not overly impressive to anyone. It is okay for a quick piece of toast, but otherwise, they were not that thrilled with it.

QUALITY OF BUILD
This seems well made and sturdy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This grill is sturdy, the burners performed well, and it seems to be well made. The grill was not that thrilling and no one wanted to use it much.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. As a basic stove, it worked great on a 1 lb tank of propane (which my husband bought by accident last year instead of butane). The grill was not why we got it, so not using it much is not that big of a deal.

Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue I looked at tons of weighted hoola hoops on Amazon and saw many of them has some not so great reviews because they were no sturdy or would break apart. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue

While riding on a slightly bumpy road with a half filled bottle in the cage, the two plastic areas at the mount points simply gave way. The fix is fairly simple but may require a quick trip to a hardware store. Using rubber washers against the plastic and metal washers against the frame (mount points) and bolt heads, the cage is now [probably] better than new. I doubt it will break again, as the new mounting method distributes weight/load more evenly across the plastic, and the rubber washers offer a bit of shock-resistance. Hopefully the manufacturer will read this, having likely heard similar reports from other customers, and fix the issue - if not done already. I still like the design and flexibility.

Original Review: The only problem here is the plastic to metal nut that tightens down to hold the sliding cage in place. I do not see that lasting for a long time. But with a trip to the hardware store I was able to get all metal parts, with washers to protect the plastic cage, hoping to avoids cracks and snaps down the road. If you only use one size container, thus unlikely to move it around, the this should work just fine.
The great thing is that this does hold nearly any bottle within the size range in place, without issue. Even when mountain biking I had no problems with the 12oz Poland Springs bottle that was in there.

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

text_fidelity_a:
iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag Guys, now this is the real deal! It is far from the standard, wimpy, light weight chairs you're used to seeing set up around camp fires or out on the soccer field sidelines. I am incredibly impressed.
The metal feels incredibly strong and durable. It's a very thick and heavy frame. If a kid or klutzy adult (like myself) were to bump hard into one of the arms or legs when someone was someone was sitting in it, it could easily leave a bruise. I'm not trying to suggest this chair isn't safe, but rather trying to convey just how heavy duty this metal frame is. Plus, the material the seat is made out of is very thick too. It also looks incredibly durable and like it should last a long time. I haven't had a reason to wash this chair yet, but I see no reason why this material wouldn't be easy clean if it needed it. Oh, and it is much more comfortable to sit in than the other chairs. The sturdiness helps an awful lot.
So overall, I really do like it. But because it is so "heavy duty" it is a heavy chair! Especially when to compared to what a standard folding chair weighs. I can't say for sure, but I suspect this chair probably weighs around twice as much as the average camping chair. Which probably isn't a big deal if you're not having to carry it a very long way. But lets say I had to hike quite a ways to a camping site (with the weight of all the other gear on my back too), well then I would think twice about choosing this chair. Oh and it is taller than most too. I would say it's about six inches taller then the standard folding chair.
So overall, I defiantly think this is an impressive, well made chair. I am 5'6 and a 150 pounds, so I already fit "comfortably" in a standard camping chair. For me personally, unless I had severe back pain or some other painful condition, I don't think I personally would NEED this chair. I still really like it and would prefer to sit in it, but a chair this heavy duty wouldn't be necessity for me. My 250 lb hubby on the other hand would completely disagree. He is VERY comfortable sitting in this chair. He also probably wouldn't noticed the extra length or weight of this chair if he had to carry it folded up on his back. Hands down, he would most certainly prefer this chair over the standard type of camping chair. It really is that nice. We both would recommend it. I'm even saving this as an idea to get my own dad for next Father's day!
text_fidelity_b: iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training I am a senior, and was exercising religiously at a fitness center, prior to the virus. I won't be going back.
We live in a senior condo, and I have no space for fitness hardware.

After almost three months of not exercising, I was getting depressed, and purchased an inexpensive set of bands from Amazon. My only prior expensive with bands was a short rehab stint for a frozen shoulder and stiff neck.

Being new to bands, I didn't know what to get,.
The inexpensive bands I bought, didn't do much for me.

I found there are three primary types of resistance bands.
The open ended rubber hose style, that can have handles attached,
The closed loop design. This product being reviewed is closed loop.
The very wide open ended bands I used in rehab. Those are very flexible and can be used open, or knotted. They don't seem to be widely available.

After buying the open ended rubber hose style, I started exercising in front of You Tube Fitness videos. In my case, senior fitness videos. Although I'm a male, I use the Senior Fitness with Meredith, exercise. No products are advertised for sale on the site. I quickly saw the advantage in having different sets of bands. There is also an advantage in having different lengths. Different exercises utilize the open ended rubber hose style, while others lend themselves to the closed loop. The thicker closed loop bands seem safer for lower body exercises. I first used the thinner rubber type bands for lower body exercises. One slipped off my foot, and boomeranged back into my throat. Ouch.

Having different sets keeps you from wasting time by having to stop and change your bands, such as removing handles and tying loops during exercises, and then untying them. Just switch to the right band.

This product being reviewed has closed loops, of varied resistance. Depending on your level of fitness, they can wear you out as you change to thicker bands. A few items in this set were an overkill for me. I won't use the jump rope or the sliders. The sliders are useful though for moving furniture. They are the same size as the large sliders I keep under my sofa, for ease of moving. The quality of the bands that come with this product seem excellent.

The items in this product can easily be returned to the original bag, taking up almost no space. Don't rip the box as it also comes in handy for storage.

Finally, if you are new to bands, I suggest watching some videos utilizing different bands, and starting with the type that appeals to you.
text_fidelity_b: 19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training

The air pressure gauge is large, easily ready ad slightly up from the bottom of the pump in a good position. When the pump arrived the indicator ring was actually set to 5 Bar, the correct pressure for the Schwalbe Kojak slick tires on my REI Ghost bike. The Air tube is on a rotating hinge on the side of the pump frame. There is a ledge for you to place the caps for your Presta Valve Stems. Nice Touch.

Using this pump to to check and reinflate my tires on my commuter bike is all it takes to keep riding safely and easily.

Of the two maintenance tasks you can do easily by yourself as a bike owner (the other being chain lubrication), keeping your tires at the recommended pressure reliably improves your bike riding.

text_fidelity_a: Fitness by Cathe' Adjustable Max Vest Here goes.. I speed walk almost every day for at 3 sometimes 5 miles. To be honest, I see others out there with hand weights and a few times I almost purchased same (trying to kick up my workout a notch). So, in the Vine program I see this one week as an eligible item and I jumped. Well, the real upside to this is that it is adjustable, so you can add and subtract weights. But, that's all that seemed to be a plus for me. On the downside, the vest comes with only one strap which is over my chest area (definitely could have used a bottom strap). I found it extremely uncomfortable while walking, with the vest shifting all around while I walked from foot to foot (and the faster I walked, the worse it got). I was wearing this under my t-shirt with just a sports bra and found it scratchy and irritating and when I sweat, it became extremely uncomfortable. I ended up wearing it over my t-shirt which, although it resolved the scratchy feel to my bare skin and some of the shifting problem, but it made me look dopey as I was walking. In fairness, I rated this a three star. I figure if you are using for mat work (pilates or weights) it would probably do the trick for extra resistance. And, as I mentioned earlier, I realy did like the ability to add and subtract weights to tailor a workout. Would definitely not recommend for walking or running.
text_fidelity_b: Fitness by Cathe' Adjustable Max Vest

If you are realistic about what this can and can't do I think it is a nice basket for a third of the price (I bought it on sale ($39) of the innova and mvp versions. If this gets a lot of use then I don't mind buying them a pricier sturdier basket.

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Strength Band I have been through a lot this last year and having the ability to do quick exercises on the go is important. I have to go slowly and work up again to build up my body due to some issues and getting these strength bands is just the thing that I needed.

WHAT ARE THESE STRENGTH BANDS LIKE?
FILA strength bands come in a pretty sturdy box (significant because you can store them in there if you like). There are three bands that are color coded so it is easy to quickly identify their strength resistance when you need to grab one. The purple is light, the blue is medium, and the gray is heavy resistance. Along with the bands which each come individually wrapped are two paper fold outs. One has tips and warnings, and the other has a few exercise ideas of what you can do with these bands. I did notice that there is not a huge offensive smell with these bands either, so I wanted to point that out for anyone who might be concerned about that.

HOW DO THESE BANDS PERFORM?
Because I have to build up slowly, I have only been able to work up to the light resistance band at this point. At first the band seems as if it will not stretch that long as I am about 5ft 7in tall. I was particularly interested in doing the exercises which use the foot and require the arms to stretch above the head extended all of the way up. As I keep using the bands, they loosen up, however, and then they are perfect for whatever exercises that I want to use them for.

MY IMPRESSIONS OF THIS PACKAGE
To be honest, although I love the bands so far, I am a bit disappointed in the lack of exercises ideas included in this kit. I really would have like it if they included more ideas of what exercises to do with this band. I do realize that it is possible to look these up on the internet to find more exercises, but I would have liked it to be included in the set.

As for the bands, so far it is easy to hold and use, and I am finding my arms and shoulders are getting stronger which is just what I wanted.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Easy to hold and work with once they are broken in, these bands are a great way to do quick exercises to build strength. Color coded for easy identification, the quality of the bands seems to be solid so far. I only wish that more exercise ideas had been included in the box.

If I could, I would give these four and a half stars, but I can't so I am giving them five stars with the statement that better insert included with more exercises would make this much nicer than it is. But the bands themselves are great, so I plan to look up more exercises.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Strength Band

text_fidelity_a:
Ringside Apex Bag Gloves, IMF-Tech Boxing Gloves with Secure Wrist Support, Synthetic Boxing Gloves for Men and Women Note: These were provided free for review, so I did not choose the size or color.

These boxing gloves came in a bright pink with neon green accents, and though I had intended to share them with my male other half, that was immediately scrapped as he was unwilling to wear such an unmanly color to work out. Good thing too, because when he tried them on, his fingers were pushing against the tips and they clearly did not fit his average sized men’s hands. If you are a man, even a smaller man, I'd recommend sizing up at LEAST to M/L but probably even larger.

As a woman, I liked these boxing gloves quite a bit. They fit my hands in an ideal fashion, gave just enough padding in just the right places that I could punch a person holding a padded shield and also use a punching bag with a reasonable amount of feedback yet absolutely no soreness or pain. Though they are brightly colored, in a workout setting that is appropriate. These are a heck of a lot nicer to use than those gross ones at the gym that everybody is allowed to use.

The one thing I didn’t like is that near the tip of the fingers, the fabric is gathered in a way that on one of my hands, feels uncomfortable. There is a thick gather of fabric right where my middle finger sets, and I found myself fidgeting with the gloves trying to unsuccessfully flatten out that bit of fabric.

Overall, these are not the most high-end gloves I’ve ever seen, but after having tried on a number of pairs, these were great in that they fit my slim hands that have long fingers very well with no pinching or discomfort, nor did they slide around during use. They seem well-made enough that I would anticipate them lasting for some time, although I do assume that anything I purchase with the express purpose of bashing it on other things may not last more than a couple years.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Apex Bag Gloves, IMF-Tech Boxing Gloves with Secure Wrist Support, Synthetic Boxing Gloves for Men and Women

text_fidelity_a:
Park Tool GP-2 Super Patch Kit I was a big fan of GP-1(no visual difference from GP-2), the older model of GP-2.
GP-1 had very reliable record from my own experience. Each patch had lasted on the working tubes for years.
I bought GP-2 before GP-1 patches ran out. First time I used it, I was totally expecting the same result then disappointed. It doesn't even last for a few miles before it start leaking the air.
I was very curious and tried to find out what's the difference. Comparing the two patches on the same inner tube by inflating it with low pressure. GP-1 stretches about the same as inner tube while GP-2 doesn't, results in forming a shape like a bottle neck. It's not hard to see if the inner tube stretches more than the patch there will be a stress on the adhesive to lose its grip at high pressure.
This can be (maybe) avoided by using over size inner tube for the tire. I see some people are happy with their results, so this maybe the reason.
GP-1 was perfect for me, it doesn't have glue that drys out(meaning always ready) and comes in very small package, good for carrying all the time.
Now I went back to carrying a spare tube and fix the hole at home with glue patch later.
I'm hoping, some day, Park brings back the GP-1, or the GP-3 having the same stretch property.
text_fidelity_b: Park Tool GP-2 Super Patch Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor Edge Game Shears - Spring Loaded with Serrated Edge and Bone-Breaking Notch for Quartering Birds, Small Game, and Fish with Nylon Belt Sheath I clean pheasants for a game preserve. Cleaning 80-90 birds in one night, by myself, is not unheard of. My husband bought me a pair of these last year as a gift. They were more expensive than the shears I'd been using and were reccomended by the salesperson where he bought them, so he figured they would be a better quality tool overall.

It was a very nice gesture on my husband's part, but these shears turned out to be a huge disappointment.

The handles are probably the absolute worst design feature on these shears! They are skinny and hard...does not offer much stability and the hard rubber becomes unbearably uncomfortable after a while. The little nubby grippy things do nothing but dig into your skin. I was beginning to form blisters by the time I'd cut the feet & wings off of 5 birds. If the handles got even a little bit slick, my grip became very unstable; hands sliding down the handle as I'd squeeze to cut through bone.

The bone notch on the blade could be designed better too; it didn't seem to be deep enough to really grab & hold onto the bone as I was cutting. Other shears have a bone notch that's almost a half-circle. It's the perfect shape to hold onto the bone & give you the best leverage to snip right through. With these shears, if you don't carefully ensure the bone is situated JUST right in the little divot before you start squeezing, the bone will just slide down the blade and you'll end up trying to cut it with the middle of the blade which tends to work poorly.

The other major issue I had with these shears is that they bound up every time I cut through feathers & skin. When cutting through wings and especially tails, they'd bind up every time. Seemed like the blades just weren't sharp enough...but brand new, they should have been! Granted, most shears will bind up if you try to cut through a huge wad of feathers all at once or go in at the wrong angle...but these did it every. single. time. A pair of child's safety scissors might have done a better job. I even tried tightening the screw in the middle since it seemed like it wasn't tight enough....because I'd squeeze the blades closed as I made my cut and the feathers would all end up packed between the blades with a 1/8 inch seperation between them. I eventually realized it wasn't a loose screw, but rather the blades were flexible enough to *bend* when they got bound up on feathers and skin. Basically, I'd have to use the shears to break through the bone, then I was better off just ripping the wings and tails off by hand to prevent getting the shears bound up on them.

I made it through about 10 birds before I'd had enough. I had raw, cramped hands and I was having to manually rip appendages off of gamebirds. I still had 60 something birds left to clean and I was already exhausted. Something was wrong with this picture. I gave up and went back to my old shears, which were cheap (about half the price of these) dull, rickety and in need of replacing.....yet compared to the struggle I'd just put up with, they made the job seem effortless.

If you're a casual hunter who just likes to go out & shoot your limit a few times a year, these shears might be more than sufficient for you. If you're using them for smaller birds like quail, or for fish, they'd probably work fine. But if you need a pair of shears that'll stand up to heavier use for extended periods of time, while still being easy to handle and comfortable to work with....these are NOT the shears to buy.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Edge Game Shears - Spring Loaded with Serrated Edge and Bone-Breaking Notch for Quartering Birds, Small Game, and Fish with Nylon Belt Sheath
